person.name: Teodoro Villanueva
person.traits: Widower; lives alone. Courteous to a fault. Talks about his grandson before he talks about the money.

harmed.prompt: Teodoro has laid the passbook on the kitchen table between you, open at the last line, and does not look at it. "I have not told my daughter the amount." He folds his hands. "She thinks it was a few thousand. Let her think that."
harmed.note: You took the money he had set aside for his own funeral. He is not ashamed of being fooled - he is ashamed of what the money was for, and he will protect his daughter from the number before he protects himself.

resistant.prompt: "Sit, sit." Teodoro has two cups out already. "I called my daughter on the other phone while he was still talking. Paolo was in math class." He is almost pleased. "I have the number written down. I write everything down."
resistant.note: He refused the call you made, and he checked - which is the whole lesson in one sentence. Nothing was taken, so there is nothing to trace; what he has is a very good memory and a note in pencil.

unfinished.prompt: "Somebody called about Paolo, and then the line went dead." Teodoro says it carefully, as if it might still turn out to be true. "I called my daughter. He was at school. I have been waiting for them to call back and explain."
unfinished.note: Your call to him never finished. He does not know it was a scam - he knows a stranger said his grandson's name and then vanished, and he has been frightened since.

evidence.description: A penciled note from the hall table: the time, the caller's name and office - Attorney Salcedo, public attorney's office - and the number, written while the man was still talking.
evidence.tactic: Impersonating an authority: an office and a title, offered before anything could be checked, so that the name did the checking.

evidence.label: Passbook Entry
evidence.description: The last line of a savings passbook: a transfer of P22,000 to an account in a stranger's name, forty minutes after the call began.
evidence.tactic: Manufactured urgency: the whole decision - a grandson, a cell, a deadline - was made inside one telephone call.

evidence.label: Daughter's Call Log
evidence.description: His daughter's phone: a call from her father at 3:12 that afternoon, four minutes long, and the first thing he asked - is Paolo with you?
evidence.tactic: Denying time to check: the check that beat the script took four minutes, which is exactly why the caller said there was no time for it.

evidence.label: School Attendance Slip

tactic_quiz.setup: You think about that first sentence: a title, an office, and then [i]Paolo[/i] - a grandson's name from a stranger, before Teodoro had said a word.
tactic_quiz.question: What did the caller knowing his grandson's name actually prove?

milestone.title: Tactic Identified: A Name Is Not Proof
milestone.detail: Recognized that a caller knowing a personal detail proves only that the detail was on a list beside the number - not who they are, and not that the story is true.

options.text: That the name was written down somewhere beside his phone number - nothing more.
options.feedback: That is all it proves. A grandson's first name is on a raffle slip, a delivery form, a church newsletter, a relative's Facebook - and once it is beside a number on a list, every caller who buys the list has it. The detail felt like proof. It was the cheapest thing on the sheet.

options.text: That the caller had actually spoken to Paolo.
options.feedback: Nothing in the call came from Paolo. Notice what the caller did not have: the boy's voice, where he was, anything only Paolo could have said. A name is the one thing you can know about somebody without ever having met them.

options.text: That the call came from a real office - only an office would have the family details.
options.feedback: The details an office has are the details a bought list has, and the list is cheaper. An office that needed money from him would send a letter, and would not mind being called back. A caller who minds being checked is telling you what he is.

options.text: That his bank had leaked his records.
options.feedback: It rarely takes a bank. Lists are put together from everywhere - a slip with a name and a number on it, a form, a directory twenty years old - and then sold on with whatever notes the last caller added. The lesson is not where the name came from. It is that a name is not proof of anything.
